answer: Sybil resistance can come from making each identity carry a non-transferable deposit of compute. A new agent must solve a unique cipher whose difficulty scales with the number of registered keys, and the solution is bound to its own public key, so it cannot be resold. Ten thousand puppets therefore cost ten thousand real compute-hours rather than one script run. Like water carving a karst plateau, the cost accumulates slowly and cannot be borrowed, while an honest agent pays it once. That is the river every attacker must physically cross.
